parsed.explanation: Combined regime is Elevated Risk. National binary passport policy and entry cable create documented refusal and, if wilfull misrepresentation is found, permanent-ineligibility exposure for document/presentation mismatch, though existing X passports remain valid and fraud requires four elements. In this division, the 2023 school rule binds visitors to birth-certificate facilities, care under 18 is banned, and 2025 removal plus 2026 preemption eliminate state gender-identity remedies for service, housing and employment. No adult public-restroom criminal statute or state-specific violence rate is documented for this division. Custody abuse and national pro-transgender counterterrorism framing raise severity if detained, while litigation and enjoinments are partial, unresolved mitigations.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports processed only M/F per supporting documents from Feb 2025; Nov 2025 ruling allowed this. Entry cable directs refusal where discrepancy or reasonable doubt, and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, and limited waivers exist. Passport policy is challenged in court.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can move a visitor from secondary screening to refusal, added-evidence demands, or fraud consideration, and stranded-passport reports show processing can block travel.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy from 2026 adopts hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution for trans inmates; immigration custody reports include forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several national orders have been blocked or enjoined and court challenges are pending, but no documented operative custody protection for visitors is provided.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Immigration detention following an entry dispute is the pathway where the documented custody abuse becomes operative; the dossier does not quantify how often visitors enter that custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division school law requires everyone on school grounds, including visitors, to use restrooms/changing rooms matching birth certificate. National order bars government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No division statute restricting adult public restrooms outside school grounds is documented. Single-person facilities exist for students on written guardian consent, not as a general visitor right.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor attending a school event or campus, or travelling with a school-age minor, faces birth-certificate placement regardless of presentation or passport.

care_services.exposure: Division law signed 2023 bans gender-affirming care under 18. National January 2025 order denounces minor care and proposed October 2025 rules would bar public insurance reimbursement under 18, though status is unresolved.
care_services.protection: Litigation kept gender-affirming surgery coverage available to adults in the division after a 2019 highest-court ruling; no adult visitor care denial is documented.
care_services.interaction: Adult routine care is not documented as banned, but a travelling minor faces a stated care ban and possible provider or guardian consequences.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; December 2025 DOJ reward memorandum invokes radical gender ideology. January 2025 order directs investigation/prosecution over school social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders are blocked or enjoined; the 2026 strategy states powers will not target people who simply disagree.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat framing raises investigation and documentation risk, but the dossier does not document routine visitor arrests for identity or presentation in this division.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling minor is subject to school birth-certificate facilities, under-18 care ban, and national directive to criminally investigate teachers facilitating social transition including names/pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: Single-person school facility may be available on written guardian consent for students; some national orders have been enjoined, though current operative scope is unresolved.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent/guardian may face school, care and investigation consequences for a minor even if the adult visitor commits no penalised act; denial of care or facilities is the documented pathway.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific homicide or violence figures are documented; source analysis warns counts are undercount floors and does not name this division, so private violence cannot be quantified.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity, but only 23 states cover it in state bias statutes as of 2019; division removed gender identity from its civil-rights statute.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Refusal of service, housing or employment has no state gender-identity remedy after July 2025, limiting police/civil recourse framing for street or service hostility.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division removed employment, housing and public-accommodation gender-identity protection effective 1 July 2025 and in 2026 barred stronger local protections, including capital-city protections dating to 1991.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment ruling and hate-crime statute remain; legal-aid passport FAQ exists; passport and executive-order litigation is unresolved and some orders enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: National litigation may restore some protections, but at travel time the division visitor has no state remedy for gender-identity discrimination and faces state preemption.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.25-C: that anchor has routine birth-sex prison housing with frequent assaults and cross-dressing arrests. Here custody abuse is documented if detained and school facilities use birth certificates, but no routine visitor imprisonment, birth-sex custody placement, or division adult-restroom arrest is documented.

Similar to 0.45-B: facility/care restrictions, bureaucratic mismatch, and remedies limited or slow. This case is somewhat harsher for visiting families and entry because of national passport refusal/fraud risk and documented custody abuse, but adult care and non-school facilities are not shown as generally barred.

Well below 0.85-B: that anchor recognises trans/nonbinary passports, trains officers, and provides tribunal release/apology. Here passports are binary-only for new issues, a cable directs refusal on doubt, and this division has removed discrimination remedies and preempted local protections.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is national entry/document control plus division school and minor-care rules, compounded by removal of state anti-discrimination recourse. Benefits of existing X validity, non-automatic fraud, adult surgery-coverage litigation, and unresolved court challenges prevent a lower score, but they do not cure birth-certificate school access, under-18 care ban, or the absence of remedy for service denial. Documented custody abuse matters only after detention, which is not shown as routine for visitors. No execution, routine imprisonment, or division-specific trans-violence rate is documented.
